Anthracnose.quote: Small brown or black spots develop on the leaves, twigs, flowers, and fruit of the mango.
Ripe fruits affected by anthracnose develop sunken, prominent, dark brown to black decay spots before or after picking.

Bacterial_Canker.quote: Initially, small black and water-soaked lesions occur on the leaves. These spots are surrounded by chlorotic margins and limited by the veins.
Lesions can appear resulting in black and cracked branches and stems, which in turn may weaken the stability of the tree.
Water-soaked, light spots appear on infected fruits. Later, they evolve into dark star-shaped craters, oozing infectious gum that attracts opportunistic pathogens.

Powdery_Mildew.quote: Grey necrotic lesions appear on the upper side of the leaf, and leaves tend to curl downwards.
Flowers and stalks can become severely infected.
The entire fruit may become covered by the mildew and may become yellow and misshapen.

Sooty_Mould.quote: Leaves, twigs and stems can also be affected.
Dark grey to black mold on fruits.
